nodes.label: APK Build (flutter build apk)
nodes.rationale: Always use the full clean sequence (flutter clean; flutter pub get; flutter build apk) — it avoids stale-cache build failures and picks up dependency/manifest changes.

nodes.label: CORS / localhost:5173
nodes.rationale: The backend only allows the origin http://localhost:5173, so a Flutter web preview build must be served on that exact port or its API calls are blocked by CORS.

nodes.label: Node Mock API Stub
nodes.rationale: A dependency-free Node stub mirrors the student API so the app can be verified locally when the Java backend is down or can't bind.

nodes.label: Held Prototype Features (password reset, email verification, OAuth, payments/audio)
nodes.norm_label: held prototype features (password reset, email verification, oauth, payments/audio)

nodes.label: Loopback Build Issue
nodes.rationale: A local loopback proxy blocks fresh Gradle/Kotlin daemons, and interrupted builds can corrupt the Kotlin incremental cache — causing 'Unable to establish loopback connection' or Kotlin 'already registered' errors.

nodes.label: android/gradle.properties Settings
nodes.rationale: org.gradle.daemon=false, kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process, and kotlin.incremental=false avoid the daemon/cache corruption caused by the loopback proxy; only needed on machines running that proxy, should be removed on a normal machine.

nodes.label: graphify Standing Rule
nodes.rationale: Build the graphify baseline in Task 1 and refresh it in Task 10, per the standing rule to update graphify whenever code changes.

nodes.label: TDD Task-by-Task Workflow (subagent-driven-development)
nodes.rationale: Each task follows write-failing-test → verify fail → minimal implementation → verify pass → commit, so every task ends green (flutter analyze clean, flutter test passing) before moving on.

nodes.label: Brand Rebrand Decision (Yalla English Hub)
nodes.rationale: The Flutter app was built 2026-09-03 mirroring the old Fluenta prototype; the web app went through a Stage 2 transformation to Yalla English Hub the mobile app knew nothing about, so this spec closes that gap by evolving the app in place rather than rebuilding.

nodes.label: Environments, Prerequisites & Risks (§9)
nodes.rationale: Two runtime environments: (A) this dev machine, where the Java backend can't bind because a local proxy intercepts the NIO loopback selector, so a Node stub API serves the student endpoint subset instead; (B) the owner's laptop running the real Spring Boot backend for the phone-over-WiFi demo, which is the source of truth.
